api_analysis.hypothesis: The primary compile error is the unused lambda block inside stft_forward_launcher. It uses __device__ annotation without --extended-lambda and captures undefined variables. Removing this dead code eliminates the first two CUDA errors. In binding, the int64 pointer type must match launcher signature (long long*), torch complex dtype should be kComplexFloat, and c10::complex<float> requires proper include. These are the root causes.
evidence: custom_ops.cu(147): error: __host__ or __device__ annotation on lambda requires --extended-lambda nvcc flag; the lambda is defined inside launcher but unused.
custom_ops.cu(168-169): enclosing-function local variables T, frames, window not in capture list; this lambda is invalid.
custom_ops_binding.cpp(78): argmin_launcher expects long long* but output.data_ptr<int64_t>() returns int64_t* (which is long int* on Linux); mismatch.
custom_ops_binding.cpp(103): torch::kComplex64 is not a member of torch; correct dtype is torch::kComplexFloat.
custom_ops_binding.cpp(115): expected primary-expression before > token due to c10::complex<float> not being recognized, likely missing include <c10/util/complex.h> or using at::ComplexFloat.
changes: Remove the unused lambda block in stft_forward_launcher (lines around 146-173).

In custom_ops_binding.cpp, change argmin_launcher signature to take long long* and cast output.data_ptr<int64_t>() to long long*; use torch::kComplexFloat for complex dtype; include <c10/util/complex.h> and update reinterpret_cast accordingly.
